workload.name: stock xv6-public forktest, 4 MiB, Bochs BIOS
workload.commandBase: XV6_LEAN=1 XV6_FIRMWARE=bochs XV6_STEPS=40000000 XV6_STOP_ON_EXPECT=1 XV6_COMMAND=$'forktest\r' XV6_EXPECT_SERIAL=$'fork test OK\n$ ' node scripts/probe-xv6-stock.mjs
workload.normalization: Remove nativeByte, nativeStats and sharedRam fields; replace rom, image and slaveImage absolute paths with <media>; retain all other report fields in original JSON order.

numericCache.change: Key the opt-in decoded-block lookup by numeric EIP and check CS, CR3 and CR4 on the entry, avoiding a four-field string allocation on each of about 21 million lookup attempts. The runner still validates positive blocks before execution.
numericCache.assessment: The opt-in native path is around parity with ordinary stepping on this workload. The small difference between these timings is not a reliable end-to-end speedup.

opcodeForms.method: A preload observes the first non-prefix opcode and following ModRM byte during each ordinary JavaScript CPU step, then counts only steps that retire an instruction. For AB and A4 it records whether an F2/F3 repeat prefix occurred. The probe guest report remains identical to ordinary execution.
opcodeForms.keyFormat: opcode hex : ModRM mode : ModRM extension for 81/83/C1; opcode hex : repeat-prefix hex for other tracked opcodes

conclusion: Removing string-key allocation recovers most opt-in dispatch overhead, but no 10x speedup has been demonstrated. Common register SHR/AND/ADD/OR immediate forms are next low-risk decoder candidates; REP STOS requires precise write and interrupt handling.
